title: G2 useful CRM: customers, contacts, deals and tasks
objective: Build the first useful browser CRM on existing Party, Account, Contact Point, Sales and Activities owners, using the existing production identity and governed gateway. No new owners, generic CRUD backend, alternative storage or additional authorization service.
deliverables: typed browser gateway client reusing published proto messages, descriptor hashes, exact owner capability versions and mutation idempotency
ordinary Customers, Deals and Tasks routes, forms, validation, loading/error/empty states, keyboard controls and permission-aware navigation
customer create/list/search/open/update, person and organization identities, contact create/list/update, optional governed account link
deal create/list/read/update/stage and task create/list/read/update/complete, with owner identity confirmed by the server session
single owner for each business entity and no frontend database, new business crates, duplicate auth or universal CRUD
tests including authenticated and unauthorized flows, invalid inputs and real PostgreSQL process persistence proof before acceptance
check exact GitHub SHA before and after CI; production-built browser and physical installation are separately evidenced
acceptance: all changed files remain within the G2 active packet; packet generation and repository navigation are in sync
customers, contact points, accounts, deals, tasks use existing governed owner contracts and exact published versions
browser sign-in, create/edit/link/stage/complete/reload workflow succeeds against live crm-api and real PostgreSQL
multi-tenant non-disclosure, denial and data persistence on service restart are demonstrated
user interface exposes neither opaque IDs nor bearer tokens, provides comprehensible error states and prevents double submissions
required exact-head CI is green before merge, main push checks pass after merge
non_goals: launch production, upgrade deployment or claims of physical pilot acceptance before G3/G5
create new CRUD engine or new domain crates, duplicate auth/storage, broad platform rearchitecture
advanced Kanban, forecasting, campaign automation, microservices or broad CI infrastructure rewrite
